concepts.title: BM25 and the inverted index
concepts.idea: BM25 ranks documents for a search: rare words count more, repeats count a little, and long documents lose points. An index finds the right documents fast.

concepts.title: nDCG@k
concepts.idea: nDCG@k scores a ranked list: each result earns its grade, shrunk by its rank, divided by the best score the same results could earn.

concepts.title: Bi-encoder vs cross-encoder
concepts.idea: A bi-encoder reads the query and each document separately, so document vectors can be saved ahead of time; a cross-encoder reads them together, so it must run once per document, per search.

concepts.title: Is 82% better than 80%?
concepts.idea: An eval score is a guess from a sample of questions, so it has error bars; two models are only different when the range of their gap stays away from zero.

concepts.title: pass@k
concepts.idea: pass@k is the chance that at least one of k generated programs passes the tests; it is estimated from n samples by counting the ways to draw k without replacement.

concepts.title: Exact match and F1
concepts.idea: Exact match checks whether an answer equals the reference after cleaning; F1 gives partial credit for the words they share.

concepts.title: Precision, recall and reciprocal rank
concepts.idea: Precision@k, recall@k and reciprocal rank grade the same ranked list in three ways: how clean the top k is, how much of the good material it found, and how early the first good result appears.

concepts.title: LLM as judge
concepts.idea: An LLM judge grades another model’s answers cheaply and agrees with experts about as often as experts agree with each other, but it has measurable biases: it favours the answer shown first and the longer answer.

concepts.title: Pairwise preference and Elo
concepts.idea: Ranking by head-to-head votes: each vote moves two ratings, Elo does it one vote at a time, and a Bradley-Terry fit uses all votes at once.
